title: Print Reading and Machine Shop Calculations
description: This course will focus on the interpretation of multi-view engineering blueprints, visualization techniques, auxiliary, section views, appraisal of revisions columns, title blocks, and bill of materials. Students will also be introduced to basic geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T) using ANSI and ISO standards, as well as calculations used to solve common problems found in print interpretation and inspection.
outcomes: Demonstrate the ability to interpret multi-view drawings and prints.
Demonstrate the ability to solve common calculations found in machine shop applications.
objectives: Define various blueprints and shop sketches
Identify projections and views used in manufacturing
Demonstrate the various uses of dimensions, tolerances, notes and symbols
Describe screw thread and gear callout information available on prints and drawings.
Demonstrate the ability to solve common calculations found in the machine shop.
content: Define various blueprints and shop sketches
Identify projections and views used in manufacturing
One, two and three view drawings
Demonstrate the various uses of dimensions, tolerances, notes and symbols
Methods and systems of dimensioning and tolerancing
Methods of machining symbols and notes
Describe screw thread and gear callout information available on prints and drawings.
Demonstrate the ability to solve common calculations found in the machine shop.
Applications of geometric and trigonometric functions.
assignments: Required reading assignments from text and supplemental handouts
Skill exercises to practice print reading and calculations assignments
Project that requires comprehension and application of calculations used to complete a process plan to interpret prints.
